correctness.rationale: Theorem 6.3 gives all shortest embeddings as \(B=U^{-1}[D;E]\) with \(D\in GL_2(R)\) and \(E\in R^{1\times2}\). The reduction map gives \(|GL_2(R)|=6\cdot16=96\), hence \(1536\) cases. The verifier enumerates all \(64\) words of every case, checks binary Gray rank \(6\), binary Gram rank \(6\), the complete \(768/720/48\) distance census, both optimal weight enumerators, and the source-displayed \(B\). No sampling or timeout is used.

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly relies on exhaustive enumeration to identify the best shortest LCD embedding in Example 7.5, but publishes only one maximizer. A complete census turns that existential optimization into a reproducible finite classification: it quantifies the rarity of the optimal Gray distance (48 of 1536), separates ring distance from Gray distance, proves every Gray image is binary LCD, and exposes two distinct optimal spectra. These are natural invariants of the exact example and materially sharpen how robust or non-unique the paper's displayed optimum is.
